job.rawJd: Fingerpaint Medical helps pharmaceutical and biotech companies communicate complex scientific data through educational programs and strategic communications that support healthcare-provider decisions, product adoption, and commercial success. The Account Supervisor is responsible for day-to-day client account management and seamless project execution. The role serves as a primary client contact, guides internal teams, and mentors junior staff. Client and account responsibilities include maintaining client relationships, explaining scopes of work, estimates, and change orders, understanding client strategy, organizations, products, disease states, medical communications, and lifecycle management, identifying strategic growth and white-space opportunities, contributing to strategy across educational and commercial initiatives, leading client meetings, anticipating questions or objections, solving complex issues, managing complex projects, and supporting workshops and brainstorming sessions. Project and financial responsibilities include owning projects from kickoff through completion, managing budgets and financial tracking, flagging budget risk, developing scopes of work, maintaining estimates and out-of-scope needs, reconciling projects, building timelines, communicating strategy and tactical plans, overseeing staff resourcing, developing project briefs and palettes, enforcing agency processes, and ensuring status reports are maintained. Team responsibilities include supervising, training, and developing direct reports, collaborating across departments, improving ways of working, supporting brand-plan development, and communicating effectively across the agency. Qualifications include a bachelor's degree in a relevant field, five to seven years of pharmaceutical or medical communications agency experience, strategic and collaborative thinking, strong organization and follow-through, communication and relationship-building skills, project-management software and business-tool proficiency, Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint proficiency, and travel three to five times per year.
